docs.text: Quick start

docs.title: A minimal ECU in one file
docs.text:
The library touches the hardware through two things you provide: a function that writes one CAN frame, and the received frames you pass in together with the current time in microseconds. Everything else — segmentation, flow control, timeouts — happens inside isotp_link_receive() and isotp_link_poll(). This program echoes every request it receives on CAN ID 0x7E0 back on 0x7E8, whatever its length:

#include "isotp.h"

static struct isotp_link link;

static int can_write(void* context, uint32_t can_id, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    return board_can_write(can_id, data, length);
}

static void on_message(const uint8_t* data, uint32_t length, void* context)
{
    (void) context;
    (void) isotp_link_send(&link, data, length, board_micros()); /* echo */
}

int main(void)
{
    struct isotp_link_config config;
    uint8_t frame[8];
    uint32_t can_id;

    isotp_link_config_default(&config);
    config.tx_id = 0x7E8U;
    config.write = can_write;
    config.on_message = on_message;
    (void) isotp_link_init(&link, &config);

    for (;;)
    {
        size_t length = board_can_read(&can_id, frame); /* 0: no frame waiting */
        if ((length > 0U) && (can_id == 0x7E0U))
        {
            isotp_link_receive(&link, frame, length, board_micros());
        }
        isotp_link_poll(&link, board_micros());
    }
}

board_can_write(), board_can_read() and board_micros() stand for your CAN driver and a free-running microsecond timer; the examples implement them for a simulated board, Linux SocketCAN and Zephyr.

struct isotp_pdu
{
    uint8_t type;
    uint32_t message_length;
    uint8_t data_offset;
    uint8_t data_length;
    uint8_t sequence_number;
    uint8_t flow_status;
    uint8_t block_size;
    uint8_t st_min;
};

docs.title: Link — isotp_link.h
docs.text:
typedef int (*isotp_can_write_fn)(void* context, uint32_t can_id, const uint8_t* data,
                                  size_t length);

Writes one CAN frame. Returns 0 when the frame is queued, ISOTP_BUSY when the driver has no free mailbox (a Consecutive Frame is retried on the next poll), any other value on a driver error. data is valid only during the call.

typedef void (*isotp_message_handler_t)(const uint8_t* data, uint32_t length, void* context);

Receives one complete message. data is valid only during the call. The handler may call isotp_link_send() on the same link.

typedef void (*isotp_result_fn)(int n_result, void* context);

Receives the N_Result of a finished transmission (on_tx_done) or of a failed reception (on_rx_error).

struct isotp_link_config
{
    uint32_t tx_id;
    isotp_can_write_fn write;
    void* write_context;
    isotp_message_handler_t on_message;
    isotp_result_fn on_tx_done;
    isotp_result_fn on_rx_error;
    void* app_context;
    uint8_t block_size;
    uint32_t st_min_us;
    uint32_t n_bs_timeout_us;
    uint32_t n_cr_timeout_us;
    uint8_t wft_max;
    bool padding;
    uint8_t padding_value;
};
Member Meaning tx_id CAN ID of every frame this link sends write, write_context Frame writer (required) and the context passed to it on_message Complete received message; NULL discards it on_tx_done End of every transmission started by isotp_link_send(); may be NULL on_rx_error Failed or interrupted reception; may be NULL app_context Context passed to the three callbacks above block_size, st_min_us BS and STmin requested from the sender (STmin 0..127 000 µs) n_bs_timeout_us, n_cr_timeout_us N_Bs and N_Cr, 1..2^31−1 µs wft_max N_WFTmax: Wait frames accepted in a row padding, padding_value Pad every sent frame to 8 bytes with this byte

struct isotp_link holds the state of one link: a copy of the configuration, both message buffers, both state machines and the invalid-frame counter. Declare it with static storage (it holds the buffers) and treat its members as private.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: This chapter explains how ISOTP-C is built: its layers, how frames and messages flow through it, the transmitter and receiver state machines with their timers, how errors are reported, and why it is designed this way.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
Layer Header Responsibility Definitions isotp_defs.h Frame types, flow status values, frame layout limits, return and N_Result codes, big-endian helpers. No state. Configuration isotp_config.h Buffer sizes and protocol defaults, range-checked at compile time. Codec isotp_protocol.h isotp_decode() validates one CAN frame and describes it in a struct isotp_pdu; isotp_encode_*() write one frame; isotp_frame_pad(); STmin conversion. Pure functions over caller buffers. Link isotp_link.h One connection to one peer: copies outgoing messages, sends FF and CFs under the receiver's flow control, reassembles incoming messages, answers with Flow Control, runs the N_Bs and N_Cr timers, reports results.

Each layer depends only on the ones below it. The codec can be used without the link, for example in a bus monitor that only decodes frames.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
Receive path. Your CAN interrupt stores the frame; your task or main loop takes it out, checks that its CAN ID belongs to this link and calls isotp_link_receive() with the current time. The link decodes the frame and acts on it. A Single Frame is delivered to on_message() straight from the frame data; the frames of a segmented message are copied into the link's receive buffer, and on_message() is called when the last byte has arrived. The link writes its Flow Control frames itself, through your write function.

Transmit path. isotp_link_send() sends a message of up to 7 bytes at once as a Single Frame. A longer message is copied into the link's transmit buffer and its First Frame is written; then the link waits for the receiver's Flow Control frame. Each call of isotp_link_poll() sends at most one Consecutive Frame, when the separation time has passed and the block is not finished. When the last frame has been written, the link calls on_tx_done(ISOTP_N_OK).

docs.title: Segmentation and flow control
docs.text:
A message that does not fit a Single Frame is sent as a First Frame, which announces the total length and carries the first 6 bytes, followed by Consecutive Frames of up to 7 bytes with a 4-bit sequence number that starts at 1 and wraps from 15 to 0. After the First Frame and after every block of BS Consecutive Frames, the sender waits for a Flow Control frame from the receiver:

Flow status Sender CTS (continue to send) Sends the next block of BS frames (BS = 0: all remaining frames) with at least STmin between two frames WAIT Keeps waiting and restarts N_Bs; more than N_WFTmax Wait frames in a row end the transmission with ISOTP_N_WFT_OVRN OVFLW (overflow) Ends the transmission with ISOTP_N_BUFFER_OVFLW other value Ends the transmission with ISOTP_N_INVALID_FS

The receiver answers a First Frame with CTS and its own BS and STmin (isotp_link_config::block_size, ::st_min_us), and repeats the CTS after every BS Consecutive Frames. It answers with OVFLW when the announced length does not fit ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE. The library never sends WAIT: its receive buffer is always ready.

docs.title: The receiver
docs.text:
1. Decode. isotp_decode() rejects what ISO 15765-2 tells a receiver to ignore: a reserved frame type, SF_DL 0 or longer than the frame, a First Frame shorter than 8 bytes or announcing a message that would fit a Single Frame, an escape-sequence First Frame with a length up to 4095, a Consecutive Frame without data, a Flow Control frame shorter than 3 bytes. Rejected frames are counted (isotp_link_invalid_frames()).
  2. Single or First Frame. If a reception is in progress, it ends with on_rx_error(ISOTP_N_UNEXP_PDU) and the new frame is processed: a Single Frame is delivered at once, a First Frame starts a new reception.
  3. Consecutive Frame. Ignored when no reception is in progress. A wrong sequence number ends the reception with ISOTP_N_WRONG_SN. A frame that carries fewer bytes than are still expected is counted as invalid and ignored. Otherwise its bytes are copied, N_Cr restarts, and the message is delivered when it is complete.
  4. Flow Control frame. Handled by the transmitter when it waits for one (see above); ignored otherwise.
  5. Timeout. isotp_link_poll() ends a reception with ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_CR when no Consecutive Frame arrived within N_Cr.

Recovery after errors

After any error the receiver is idle and accepts the next Single or First Frame. ISO-TP has no retransmission: the sender learns about a receiver error only by its own timeout (N_Bs) or by an Overflow, and the application (for example the UDS client) repeats the request.

docs.title: The transmitter
docs.text:
State Entered when Leaves on ISOTP_TX_IDLE init, end of a transmission isotp_link_send() of more than 7 bytes ISOTP_TX_WAIT_FC First Frame written; block of BS frames written FC CTS → SEND_CF; FC WAIT (≤ N_WFTmax) → stays; FC OVFLW, invalid FS, too many WAIT, N_Bs expired → IDLE with an error ISOTP_TX_SEND_CF FC CTS received last frame written → IDLE (ISOTP_N_OK); block done → WAIT_FC; write error → IDLE (ISOTP_N_ERROR)

When the write function returns ISOTP_BUSY for a Consecutive Frame, the link tries the same frame again on the next poll. For a Single or First Frame, isotp_link_send() returns the writer's result and nothing is started.

docs.title: Time
docs.text: The library never reads a clock. Every call that can start or check a timer takes now_us, a free-running microsecond counter that may wrap at 2^32. Deadlines are stored as now_us + timeout and compared modulo 2^32, which is correct as long as a timeout is shorter than 2^31 µs (about 35 minutes); isotp_link_init() enforces that. The resolution you get is the resolution of your counter and of your poll interval: to send at an STmin of 1 ms, poll at least every millisecond.

docs.title: Memory model
docs.text:
Structure Contents Size with the default configuration (Cortex-M4) struct isotp_link configuration copy, both message buffers, both state machines, counters 8 296 bytes struct isotp_link_config CAN ID, callbacks, flow-control and timing parameters 48 bytes struct isotp_pdu one decoded frame (on the stack inside the link) 16 bytes Frame buffer 8 bytes on the stack while one frame is written 8 bytes

There is no global state. Every link is independent; an application with three peers declares three links.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Situation Result A NULL pointer, zero length or a value out of range ISOTP_ERROR; nothing is written or changed isotp_link_send() while a segmented transmission is in progress ISOTP_BUSY The write function fails on a Single or First Frame Its return value is returned by isotp_link_send() The write function fails on a Consecutive Frame ISOTP_BUSY: retried on the next poll; other: on_tx_done(ISOTP_N_ERROR) The write function fails on a Flow Control frame on_rx_error(ISOTP_N_ERROR); the reception ends Malformed frame Ignored, isotp_link_invalid_frames() + 1 Protocol error or timeout on_tx_done() / on_rx_error() with the N_Result code; also readable with isotp_link_tx_result() / isotp_link_rx_result()

docs.title: Threading and reentrancy
docs.text:
• Codec functions are reentrant: they only touch their arguments.
  • A link is not thread-safe. Call isotp_link_receive(), isotp_link_poll() and isotp_link_send() of one link from one context — a CAN task or the main loop, not the CAN interrupt — or protect all three with one mutex.
  • Callbacks run in the caller's context, inside isotp_link_receive(), isotp_link_poll() or isotp_link_send(). They may call isotp_link_send() on the same link: the link updates its state before it calls them.
  • The message data passed to on_message() is valid only during the call.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason Time is an argument (now_us) No dependency on an OS or timer driver; tests control time exactly; works with any clock source. One Consecutive Frame per poll Bounded execution time per call; the CAN driver's queue is never flooded; STmin below the poll interval is still met because frames are never sent early. The link copies outgoing messages The caller may reuse its buffer at once; no lifetime rules for the payload. Buffers sized at build time No heap; the RAM per link is known at link time and in the map file. STmin rounded up when encoded The sender is never asked to go faster than the receiver needs. Reserved STmin values read as 127 ms Required by ISO 15765-2 for senders. Single Frame delivered from the frame No copy for the most common case (short requests). Separate write and application contexts The driver and the application layer are usually different modules. Functional addressing only for Single Frames ISO 15765-2 does not allow segmented messages to functional addresses.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to this project are documented in this file. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

Version 2.0.0 was tagged but not published as a GitHub Release, and its tag cannot be reused. 2.0.1 is the first published release of version 2: it contains every change listed under 2.0.0 and the fixes below. The library code is unchanged.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The documentation is deployed after the Release workflow of a vX.Y.Z tag, from the tagged commit, instead of after every build on main.
  • The documentation is pushed to gh-pages with the deploy key again; the gh-pages ruleset rejects pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN.
Version 2 is a rewrite of the library to the SystemFromScratch® protocol-library standard. The public API changed; the wire format is ISO 15765-2 as before.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Layered library: isotp_defs.h (constants, N_Result codes), isotp_protocol.h (frame codec: isotp_decode(), isotp_encode_*(), isotp_frame_pad(), STmin) and isotp_link.h (transport layer), each usable on its own.
  • Explicit time input: every link call takes now_us; the library no longer calls isotp_user_get_us() or any other platform function.
  • struct isotp_link_config with run-time block size, STmin, N_Bs, N_Cr, N_WFTmax and padding per link; isotp_link_config_default().
  • Callbacks with a context: on_message(), on_tx_done() (every transmission, with its N_Result) and on_rx_error().
  • isotp_link_send_functional() for functional (broadcast) Single Frames.
  • Diagnostics: isotp_link_tx_busy(), isotp_link_tx_result(), isotp_link_rx_result(), isotp_link_invalid_frames().
  • Examples: bare-metal UDS-style ECU with a simulated tester (CTest), Linux SocketCAN request tool, Zephyr application.
  • Python twin of the codec with a C/Python cross-check and end-to-end tests of the C link against the twin.
  • Documentation website in the SystemFromScratch® style, MISRA deviation register, measured RAM and stack figures, CITATION.cff, release workflow.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking: IsoTpLink is now struct isotp_link; isotp_init_link(), isotp_on_can_message(), isotp_send(), isotp_poll() are replaced by isotp_link_init(), isotp_link_receive(), isotp_link_send(), isotp_link_poll().
  • Breaking: the message buffers are part of struct isotp_link, sized by ISOTP_TX_BUFFER_SIZE and ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE, instead of caller pointers.
  • Breaking: received messages are delivered to on_message(); the polled isotp_receive() and the weak isotp_user_*() functions are removed.
  • Breaking: configuration macros renamed from ISO_TP_* to ISOTP_*; the compile-time switches for callbacks, padding and the send argument are now run-time configuration.
  • Return codes reduced to ISOTP_OK, ISOTP_ERROR, ISOTP_BUSY; protocol outcomes use the ISOTP_N_* N_Result codes.
  • One Consecutive Frame per isotp_link_poll() call, with wrap-safe timers.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The 32-bit FF_DL is encoded and decoded big-endian on every host (it was byte-swapped only on little-endian hosts).
  • Reserved STmin values are treated as 127 ms, as ISO 15765-2 requires (they were 0).
  • The requested STmin is rounded up when encoded, never down.
  • Flow Control frames are only accepted while the sender waits for one; an escape First Frame announcing 4095 bytes or less is ignored.
  • Segmented transmissions are no longer allowed to functional addresses.
  • The N_Cr timer works when the deadline is 0 after a clock wrap.
  • No <stdio.h>, snprintf() or assert() in the library.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• 82 unit tests, 100 % line and branch coverage of src/ (gate in CI).
  • 62 integration tests (pytest) against the Python twin.
  • Cppcheck MISRA C:2012 addon: 0 violations (gate in CI); 3 documented advisory deviations.

docs.title: 1.6.0 and earlier
docs.text: Versions 1.x of the fork kept the API of isotp-c by Li Shen and Simon Cahill. See the Git history and the releases.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Build-time parameters live in inc/isotp_config.h. Each one is guarded by #ifndef and range-checked at compile time; override it with a compiler definition, for example -DISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE=256U. The two buffer sizes are compiled into struct isotp_link; the other values are only the defaults that isotp_link_config_default() writes into a struct isotp_link_config, so every link can use its own values at run time.

Parameter Default Range Meaning ISOTP_TX_BUFFER_SIZE 4095U 8 … 2^31−1 Largest message a link sends, in bytes ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE 4095U 8 … 2^31−1 Largest message a link receives; longer ones are refused with FC OVFLW ISOTP_DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE 8U 0 … 255 BS this receiver requests; 0 = no further Flow Control ISOTP_DEFAULT_ST_MIN_US 0U 0 … 127000 STmin this receiver requests, µs ISOTP_DEFAULT_N_BS_TIMEOUT_US 1000000U 1 … 2^31−1 N_Bs, µs (ISO 15765-2: 1000 ms) ISOTP_DEFAULT_N_CR_TIMEOUT_US 1000000U 1 … 2^31−1 N_Cr, µs (ISO 15765-2: 1000 ms) ISOTP_DEFAULT_WFT_MAX 10U 0 … 255 N_WFTmax: Wait frames accepted in a row

Messages longer than 4095 bytes use the 32-bit FF_DL of ISO 15765-2:2016; they need a buffer size above 4095. Your peer must support the escape sequence too.

docs.title: Run-time configuration
docs.text:
struct isotp_link_config also holds what has no build-time default:

Member Default Meaning tx_id 0 CAN ID of every frame this link sends (11- or 29-bit, passed to the writer) write, write_context none Frame writer (required) and its context on_message, on_tx_done, on_rx_error, app_context none Callbacks and their context padding, padding_value false, 0xCC Pad every sent frame to 8 bytes

isotp_link_init() rejects a configuration without a writer, an STmin above 127 000 µs and timeouts of 0 or above 2^31−1 µs (deadlines are compared modulo 2^32).

docs.title: Memory footprint
docs.text:
Measured with sizeof and arm-none-eabi-size (Cortex-M4, -Os):

Object Size struct isotp_link, default 4095-byte buffers 8 296 bytes struct isotp_link, 256-byte buffers 616 bytes struct isotp_link, 64-byte buffers 232 bytes Per link without the buffers 104 bytes struct isotp_link_config 48 bytes Code: isotp_protocol.o + isotp_link.o 516 + 1 268 = 1 784 bytes of flash, no data, no bss

The library has no global variables: the RAM it uses is the struct isotp_link instances you declare (one per peer) and the stack.

docs.title: Bare metal
docs.text:
A UDS-style ECU on request ID 0x7E0 (and functional ID 0x7DF) that answers on 0x7E8. It supports TesterPresent, and reading and writing a 17-byte VIN with Read/WriteDataByIdentifier 0xF190 — so the response to a read and the write request are both segmented — and answers other services with a negative response.

File Contents examples/bare_metal/main.c The ECU: CAN RX interrupt → ring buffer → main loop → link → services examples/bare_metal/board.h The four functions to port: board_init(), board_can_write(), board_micros(), board_idle() examples/bare_metal/board_host.c Simulated board for the PC: a tester with its own link on a virtual bus

The ECU asks for a block size of 2 and an STmin of 1 ms; the simulated tester asks for a block size of 4 and an STmin of 2 ms, so both directions use several Flow Control frames. Before every request the tester injects a malformed frame on the request ID and a frame of another node. The program exits with 0 when every response matches. Real output:

docs.title: Linux SocketCAN
docs.text:
isotp_request sends one request from a PC and prints the response:

isotp_request can0 7E0 7E8 22 F1 90
File Contents examples/linux_socketcan/main.c Raw CAN socket with a filter on the response ID, poll() every millisecond, CLOCK_MONOTONIC

It pads frames to 8 bytes, waits up to 2 s for the response and prints the N_Result on an error. Without hardware, create a virtual bus with sudo ip link add dev vcan0 type vcan && sudo ip link set up vcan0 and run an ECU on it.

docs.title: Zephyr
docs.text:
The ECU on the Zephyr CAN API, for the CAN controller chosen as zephyr,canbus:

west build -b <board> examples/zephyr
File Contents examples/zephyr/src/main.c Filters for 0x7E0/0x7DF into a k_msgq, one thread that feeds and polls the link every millisecond, can_send() with -EAGAIN mapped to ISOTP_BUSY examples/zephyr/CMakeLists.txt Includes isotp.cmake and links the library to zephyr_interface examples/zephyr/prj.conf CONFIG_CAN=y, no heap

It answers TesterPresent and replies serviceNotSupported to everything else; add your services in on_request().

docs.title: Extending the Library
docs.text: Almost everything an application needs is built on top of ISOTP-C: a different CAN driver, more peers, diagnostic services, gateways. This chapter shows where each kind of extension belongs, what would need a library change, and how to contribute one.

docs.title: Where to extend
docs.text: You want to… Do it in Library change needed? Use another CAN driver or controller your write function and receive loop No Talk to several ECUs one struct isotp_link per peer, route frames by CAN ID No Use 29-bit CAN IDs (for example normal fixed addressing 0x18DAxxyy) tx_id and your routing; the writer sets the IDE flag No Implement UDS, OBD or a bootloader on_message() and the application No Route ISO-TP between two buses (gateway) two links and the application No Change buffer sizes or defaults compiler definitions, see Configuration No Extended or mixed addressing (address byte before N_PCI) the codec and the link Yes CAN FD (frames of up to 64 bytes) the codec and the link Yes Several messages in flight per link not planned: ISO-TP is one message per direction per link —

docs.title: Adding a CAN driver
docs.text:
The write function receives the CAN ID and 1 to 8 data bytes and must return:

Return Meaning for the link 0 The frame is queued for transmission ISOTP_BUSY No free transmit mailbox: a Consecutive Frame is retried on the next poll; isotp_link_send() returns it for a Single or First Frame any other value Driver error: a transmission ends with ISOTP_N_ERROR, a reception with ISOTP_N_ERROR when a Flow Control frame cannot be sent

The data is only valid during the call: copy it into the mailbox or your queue. Do not block for long — the link calls the writer from isotp_link_receive() to send Flow Control, and a slow writer delays the frames behind it.

docs.title: Talking to several ECUs
docs.text:
Declare one link per peer and dispatch on the CAN ID:

static struct isotp_link engine;
static struct isotp_link brake;

void on_can_frame(uint32_t can_id, const uint8_t* data, size_t length, uint32_t now_us)
{
    if (can_id == 0x7E8U)
    {
        isotp_link_receive(&engine, data, length, now_us);
    }
    else if (can_id == 0x7E9U)
    {
        isotp_link_receive(&brake, data, length, now_us);
    }
    else
    {
        /* not ISO-TP traffic for us */
    }
}

Poll every link from the same loop.

docs.title: Adding an addressing mode or CAN FD
docs.text: Both change the frame layout: extended and mixed addressing put an address byte in front of the N_PCI, CAN FD allows frames of up to 64 bytes with an escape sequence for the Single Frame length. A contribution would add the layout to struct isotp_link_config (so one build serves all modes), extend isotp_decode() and the encoders with the offset and the maximum frame length, extend the Python twin the same way, and add the reference frames of the standard to the unit and integration tests.

docs.title: Contributing to the library
docs.text:
1. Code. C11, no new dependencies, no heap, the MISRA rules used in the code (one return per function, parenthesized expressions, (void) casts, no pointer arithmetic).
  2. Tests. A unit test for every behavior; 100 % line and branch coverage; update the Python twin and the integration tests when the wire format changes.
  3. Analysis. misra-analyze reports 0 violations, or the deviation is in the register.
  4. Format. clang-format reports no changes.
  5. Documentation. The affected pages, the stack table, the diagrams (tools/docs/diagrams.py) and CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased].
  6. Compatibility. The public API is stable within a major version.

python -m pytest tests/integration -v

docs.title: Integration Guide
docs.text:
The library does not touch hardware and does not read a clock. An integration has three parts:

  1. Receive: move every CAN frame of the peer's CAN ID into isotp_link_receive(), together with the current time, from a task or the main loop — not from the CAN interrupt handler.
  2. Transmit: a write function that queues one CAN frame, and regular calls of isotp_link_poll() with the current time.
  3. Application: on_message() for complete messages, and optionally on_tx_done() and on_rx_error() for results.

Complete, buildable programs for each pattern are described in Examples.

docs.title: The time source
docs.text: now_us is any free-running microsecond counter that wraps at 2^32: a 32-bit timer running at 1 MHz, k_cyc_to_us_floor32(k_cycle_get_32()) on Zephyr, the DWT cycle counter divided by the core clock in MHz, or clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) on Linux. A millisecond tick multiplied by 1000 also works when your STmin and timeouts are whole milliseconds; the library only needs the value to grow monotonically and wrap at 2^32.

docs.title: RTOS: interrupt, queue and CAN task
docs.text:
CAN RX interrupt ──► message queue ──► CAN task ──► isotp_link_receive() ──► on_message()
                                         │
                                         └──► every 1 ms: isotp_link_poll() ──► write()

The interrupt copies the frame (ID, length, data) into a queue and returns. The CAN task waits on the queue with a timeout of one millisecond, passes each frame of the peer's ID to the link, and polls the link after every wake-up. Only this task touches the link, so no mutex is needed. When another task must send, either hand the message to the CAN task through a second queue, or protect isotp_link_send(), isotp_link_receive() and isotp_link_poll() of that link with one mutex.

docs.title: Adding the library to a CMake build
docs.text:
include(path/to/isotp-c/isotp.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE isotp)
target_link_libraries(isotp PUBLIC zephyr_interface)   # Zephyr applications only

Override the configuration on the target, for example target_compile_definitions(isotp PUBLIC ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE=512U); PUBLIC makes the application see the same struct isotp_link size as the library.

docs.title: Bare metal and host
docs.text:
Bare metal. The CAN interrupt fills a small ring buffer of frames; the main loop drains it, feeds the link and polls it, then sleeps until the next interrupt. A periodic timer interrupt (for example SysTick at 1 kHz) wakes the loop often enough for STmin and the timeouts. The bare-metal example shows the complete program.

Linux. Use SocketCAN: a raw CAN_RAW socket with a filter on the peer's ID, poll() with a timeout of one millisecond, and clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC). The kernel also has its own ISO-TP socket (CAN_ISOTP); ISOTP-C is useful on Linux when you need the same code as on the ECU, or full control over timing in a test bench.

docs.title: Notes from hardware bring-up
docs.text:
• Padding. Many ECUs and testers expect every frame to have 8 data bytes. If the peer ignores your frames, set padding = true.
  • Acceptance filters. Configure the CAN controller to accept the peer's ID (and the functional ID in an ECU); everything else costs interrupt time.
  • Transmit mailboxes. With one mailbox and STmin 0, Consecutive Frames leave as fast as the bus allows; return ISOTP_BUSY when the mailbox is full and the link retries.
  • Frame order. Use a single transmit FIFO or one mailbox for ISO-TP: priority-based mailboxes can send Consecutive Frames out of order, which the receiver reports as a wrong sequence number.
  • RX overruns. A receiver that asks for STmin 0 and BS 0 receives frames back to back (about 4 000 frames per second at 500 kbit/s): make the RX queue deep enough or ask for a block size.

docs.title: MISRA C:2012 compliance
docs.text: This page records how the library is checked against MISRA C:2012 and every deviation from it. It covers the library code only: src/, inc/ and isotp.h. Tests, examples and tools are not in scope.

docs.title: Checking
docs.text:
Check Where Gate Cppcheck MISRA C:2012 addon misra-analyze target, CI job MISRA C:2012 Analysis Fails on any violation Cppcheck, all checks cppcheck-analyze target, CI job Cppcheck Analysis Report CodeQL cpp-queries codeql-analyze target, CI job CodeQL Analysis Report Compiler -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion No warnings Manual review Pull request review, see .github/.copilot-instructions.md Reviewer

misra-analyze fails when the report contains a violation. Set -DISOTP_MISRA_FAIL_ON_VIOLATION=OFF to get the report without failing the build. A violation that cannot be fixed must be added to the deviation register below before the pull request is merged. The gate was verified by adding an early return (Rule 15.5): the target reported the violation and failed.

The Cppcheck addon checks most decidable rules, but not the directives or rules that need knowledge of the whole program or the intent of the code. Those are covered by the manual review notes below.

docs.title: Manual review notes
docs.text: Guideline How the library complies Dir 4.1 (run-time failures) Every copy into a message buffer is bounded by an invariant written next to it: a First Frame is only accepted when its FF_DL fits ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE, and every Consecutive Frame copies at most the bytes still missing. isotp_link_send() rejects messages longer than ISOTP_TX_BUFFER_SIZE. inc/isotp_config.h rejects sizes and defaults out of range at compile time. Time arithmetic is unsigned and wraps by design; deadlines are compared modulo 2^32. Dir 4.11 (validity of arguments) Every public function checks its pointer arguments, lengths and ranges and returns ISOTP_ERROR (or ignores the call, for the void functions; the accessors return a neutral value for NULL). The inline big-endian helpers in isotp_defs.h take a pointer to four readable bytes, like memcpy(). Dir 4.12, Rule 21.3 (dynamic memory) No heap. All state is in the caller-owned struct isotp_link. Rule 15.5 (single point of exit) Every function has one return at the end. Rule 17.2 (recursion) No recursion; the stack depth is fixed, see Configuration. A callback that calls back into the same link (for example isotp_link_send() from on_message()) is a bounded, one-level re-entry. Rule 21.6 (standard I/O) No <stdio.h>. The library includes only <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h> and <string.h>.

docs.title: DEV-01: int as the status type (Dir 4.6, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: return type of isotp_decode(), the isotp_encode_*() functions, isotp_frame_pad(), isotp_link_init(), isotp_link_send(), isotp_link_send_functional(), isotp_link_tx_result(), isotp_link_rx_result(), of the isotp_can_write_fn callback and the N_Result argument of isotp_result_fn.
  • Rationale: the value is a status code (ISOTP_OK, ISOTP_ERROR, ISOTP_BUSY, an N_Result code, a frame length of at most 8, or the code the write callback returned), not a quantity whose size matters. int lets an integrator return the error code of an existing CAN driver from the write callback without a conversion. int is at least 16 bits on every conforming compiler, which holds every value the library returns.
  • Risk control: the library never does arithmetic on these values; it compares them with the named codes or uses a frame length (1..8) that the encoders produced.

docs.title: DEV-02: macros not used inside the library (Rule 2.5, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_A in inc/isotp_defs.h, ISOTP_VERSION_* in isotp.h.
  • Rationale: these are the public names of protocol values and configuration. They are used by applications; ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_A is kept so that the N_Result set of ISO 15765-2 is complete even though the library writes synchronously and never produces it.

docs.title: DEV-03: external functions referenced in one translation unit (Rule 8.7, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: the public API functions that the library itself does not call, for example isotp_link_tx_busy(), isotp_link_invalid_frames() and the codec functions that only the link calls.
  • Rationale: they are the library interface and are called by applications. Giving them internal linkage would remove them from the API.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
ISOTP-C is a C11 library that implements the transport protocol of ISO 15765-2 (ISO-TP) for classical CAN, for embedded systems that must be predictable and reviewable. It carries messages of up to 4095 bytes — or longer, with the 32-bit length of ISO 15765-2:2016 — over CAN frames of eight bytes, which is what diagnostics (UDS, ISO 14229), OBD and CAN bootloaders need.

ISOTP-C started as a fork of the MIT-licensed isotp-c by Li Shen and Simon Cahill. Version 2 is a rewrite with a new API; see the changelog for the differences.

docs.title: What the library does
docs.text:
• Encodes and decodes frames. Single, First, Consecutive and Flow Control frames, including the 32-bit FF_DL escape, optional padding, and the STmin encoding with its reserved values.
  • Segments and reassembles messages. A link sends a long message as a First Frame followed by Consecutive Frames, at the block size and separation time the receiver asks for, and reassembles incoming messages while checking every sequence number.
  • Detects protocol errors. Timeouts N_Bs and N_Cr, wrong sequence numbers, unexpected frames, too many Wait frames, overflow and unknown flow status are reported as the N_Result codes of ISO 15765-2.
  • Connects the protocol to any CAN driver. One write callback; received frames and the current time are function arguments.

docs.title: What the library does not do
docs.text: Concern Why it is not in the library CAN drivers, acceptance filters Hardware- and OS-specific; you pass frames in and provide a write function. Routing CAN IDs to links Depends on your addressing plan; one link serves one pair of CAN IDs. Clocks and timers The library never reads a clock: every call takes now_us. Threads, queues, interrupts, locking Every system has its own; see the integration guide. Diagnostic services (UDS, OBD) Application layer; the examples show a small UDS-style ECU. Extended/mixed addressing, CAN FD Not implemented yet; see Extending the Library.

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
• ECU firmware. A diagnostic server or bootloader on a microcontroller, bare metal or under an RTOS.
  • Testers and gateways. A diagnostic client on a PC (SocketCAN) or a gateway that routes ISO-TP between buses.
  • Test benches. Simulated nodes that need a protocol implementation with deterministic timing (the time is an argument, so tests control it).

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Link One ISO-TP connection to one peer: the CAN ID this node sends with and the frames the application routes to it. struct isotp_link holds its state. Message (N_SDU) The payload the application sends or receives, 1 to ISOTP_TX/RX_BUFFER_SIZE bytes. SF, FF, CF, FC Single Frame, First Frame, Consecutive Frame and Flow Control frame — the four frame types (N_PDU) of ISO 15765-2. FF_DL, SF_DL The message length announced in a First Frame or Single Frame. SN Sequence number of a Consecutive Frame, 1, 2, … 15, 0, 1, … BS, STmin Block size and minimum separation time: how many Consecutive Frames the sender may send before the next Flow Control frame, and how long it waits between them. N_Bs, N_Cr Sender timeout waiting for Flow Control; receiver timeout waiting for the next Consecutive Frame. N_WFTmax How many Flow Control frames with the status Wait in a row the sender accepts. Physical and functional addressing A request to one node, or a broadcast request (only as a Single Frame).

docs.title: Conventions in this documentation
docs.text:
• Hexadecimal bytes without prefix inside frames (10 14 00 01), with 0x in text and code.
  • The 32-bit FF_DL is big-endian, as on the wire.
  • Times are in microseconds (_us) unless a unit is given.
  • ISOTP_TX_BUFFER_SIZE and ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE are shown with their default, 4095.

docs.title: ISO 15765-2 (ISO-TP)
docs.text: This chapter describes the ISO 15765-2 wire format for classical CAN with normal addressing and exactly what ISOTP-C does with each part of it. The normative reference is the standard; ISOTP-C includes the 32-bit message length introduced by the 2016 edition.

docs.title: The bus
docs.text: ISO-TP runs on top of CAN. Each direction between two nodes uses its own CAN ID — in diagnostics, for example, the tester sends to an ECU on 0x7E0 and the ECU answers on 0x7E8 — and a functional ID (0x7DF) addresses all ECUs at once. One ISOTP-C link is one such pair of IDs: it sends with tx_id, and the application gives it the frames of the peer's ID. Both directions of a link work at the same time (full duplex).

docs.title: Frames
docs.text:
The first byte, or the first two bytes, of every frame are the protocol control information (N_PCI). Its high nibble is the frame type:

Type Byte 0 Further N_PCI Data Use Single Frame (SF) 0 | SF_DL — 1..7 bytes A whole message of up to 7 bytes First Frame (FF) 1 | FF_DL bits 11..8 byte 1: FF_DL bits 7..0 6 bytes Start of a message of 8..4095 bytes First Frame, escape 10 byte 1 00, bytes 2..5: FF_DL, 32 bit, big-endian 2 bytes Start of a message of more than 4095 bytes Consecutive Frame (CF) 2 | SN — 1..7 bytes Next part of the message Flow Control (FC) 3 | FS byte 1: BS, byte 2: STmin — The receiver's answer to an FF and after every block

A First Frame is always 8 bytes long. The last Consecutive Frame carries the remaining bytes; with padding, the rest of the frame is filled with the padding byte.

docs.title: Flow status, block size and separation time
docs.text:
Field Values Meaning FS 0 CTS, 1 WAIT, 2 OVFLW Continue to send / wait for the next FC / message too long for the receiver BS 0 … 255 Consecutive Frames the sender may send before the next FC; 0: all STmin 00 … 7F Minimum time between two Consecutive Frames, 0..127 ms STmin F1 … F9 100..900 µs STmin other values Reserved; a sender treats them as 7F (127 ms)

isotp_st_min_encode() rounds a requested time up to the next value that can be encoded, so the sender never goes faster than asked; isotp_st_min_decode() maps the reserved values to 127 ms.

docs.title: Timers and N_Result
docs.text:
Timer Side Runs from … to … Default On expiry N_Bs Sender FF or last CF of a block written → FC received 1000 ms ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_BS N_Cr Receiver FC written or CF received → next CF received 1000 ms ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_CR

ISO 15765-2 also defines N_As/N_Ar (time for the CAN driver to send a frame) and the performance times N_Br/N_Cs. ISOTP-C writes frames synchronously through your write function, so it does not time them: ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_A is never produced.

N_Result Reported when ISOTP_N_OK The message was sent or received completely ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_BS No Flow Control frame within N_Bs ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_CR No Consecutive Frame within N_Cr ISOTP_N_WRONG_SN A Consecutive Frame with an unexpected sequence number ISOTP_N_INVALID_FS A Flow Control frame with an unknown flow status ISOTP_N_UNEXP_PDU A Single or First Frame interrupted a reception ISOTP_N_WFT_OVRN More than N_WFTmax Flow Control frames with WAIT in a row ISOTP_N_BUFFER_OVFLW Sender: the receiver answered OVFLW. Receiver: the announced message is longer than ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE ISOTP_N_ERROR The write function failed while sending a frame

docs.title: Receiver behavior
docs.text:
What the receiver of ISOTP-C does with every frame, following ISO 15765-2:

Frame Condition Action any Reserved type, SF_DL 0 or longer than the frame, FF not 8 bytes, FF_DL ≤ 7, escape FF_DL ≤ 4095, CF without data, FC shorter than 3 bytes Ignored, counted as invalid SF — Delivered; a reception in progress ends with N_UNEXP_PDU FF FF_DL fits the buffer FC CTS sent, reception starts; a reception in progress ends with N_UNEXP_PDU FF FF_DL too long FC OVFLW sent, N_BUFFER_OVFLW CF No reception in progress Ignored CF Wrong SN Reception ends with N_WRONG_SN CF Fewer data bytes than still expected Ignored, counted as invalid FC Not waiting for FC Ignored

Frames longer than needed (padding) are accepted in every case.

docs.text: Feature of ISO 15765-2 ISOTP-C Normal addressing, 11- and 29-bit CAN IDs Yes Normal fixed addressing (29-bit IDs with source and target address) Yes, through tx_id and your routing Extended and mixed addressing No Classical CAN (8 bytes) Yes CAN FD (up to 64 bytes) No 32-bit FF_DL (messages > 4095 bytes) Yes Functional addressing Single Frames, as required Sending FC WAIT No (the receive buffer is always ready)

docs.title: Using the Library
docs.text: A link is used the same way in an ECU (diagnostic server) and in a tester (diagnostic client): the ECU waits for requests and answers them, the tester sends a request and waits for the answer. This chapter shows both, how to use the codec on its own, what every function returns, and the mistakes that are easy to make.

docs.title: Setting up a link
docs.text:
Start from the defaults, set the CAN ID this node sends with and the callbacks, and initialize the link. The link keeps a copy of the configuration.

static struct isotp_link link;

static int can_write(void* context, uint32_t can_id, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    return board_can_write(can_id, data, length);
}

static void on_message(const uint8_t* data, uint32_t length, void* context)
{
    (void) data;
    (void) length;
    (void) context;
}

int setup(void)
{
    struct isotp_link_config config;

    isotp_link_config_default(&config);
    config.tx_id = 0x7E8U;          /* this ECU answers on 0x7E8 */
    config.write = can_write;
    config.on_message = on_message;
    config.block_size = 8U;         /* ask the tester for Flow Control every 8 frames */
    config.st_min_us = 1000U;       /* and 1 ms between its Consecutive Frames */
    config.padding = true;          /* most vehicles expect 8-byte frames */
    return isotp_link_init(&link, &config);
}

The link does not filter CAN IDs. Give it only the frames of its peer: in an ECU the physical request ID (0x7E0 above) and, if used, the functional ID (0x7DF); in a tester the response ID of the ECU.

docs.title: Writing an ECU
docs.text: An ECU calls isotp_link_receive() for every frame of its request IDs and isotp_link_poll() regularly, both with the current time. Requests arrive in on_message().

docs.title: Answering
docs.text:
Answer from on_message() or later from the application, with isotp_link_send(). The answer is copied, so a local buffer is fine:

static struct isotp_link link;

static void on_message(const uint8_t* data, uint32_t length, void* context)
{
    (void) context;
    if ((length >= 1U) && (data[0] == 0x3EU))   /* UDS TesterPresent */
    {
        const uint8_t answer[2] = {0x7EU, 0x00U};
        (void) isotp_link_send(&link, answer, sizeof(answer), board_micros());
    }
}

isotp_link_send() returns ISOTP_BUSY while a previous long answer is still being sent. A request–response protocol such as UDS never has two answers in flight; if your application can, keep the second answer and send it from on_tx_done().

docs.title: Rules a well-behaved ECU follows
docs.text:
• Poll the link at least as often as the shortest separation time a tester may ask for — usually every millisecond.
  • Answer within the time the application protocol allows (UDS: P2server, 50 ms by default); a long answer only has to start in time.
  • Do not answer functional requests that do not need an answer: this is decided by the application layer, not by ISO-TP.
  • Keep the receive buffer as large as the longest request you accept; longer requests are refused with Flow Control Overflow.

docs.title: Writing a tester
docs.text:
A tester sends a request and waits for the answer or for an error:

static struct isotp_link tester;
static volatile bool done;

static void on_answer(const uint8_t* data, uint32_t length, void* context)
{
    (void) data;
    (void) length;
    (void) context;
    done = true;
}

static void on_error(int n_result, void* context)
{
    (void) context;
    if (n_result != ISOTP_N_OK)
    {
        done = true;    /* timeout, overflow, wrong SN, ... */
    }
}

int request_vin(void)
{
    static const uint8_t request[3] = {0x22U, 0xF1U, 0x90U};   /* ReadDataByIdentifier */
    uint8_t frame[8];
    uint32_t can_id;
    const uint32_t start = board_micros();
    int result = isotp_link_send(&tester, request, sizeof(request), start);

    done = false;
    while ((result == ISOTP_OK) && !done && ((board_micros() - start) < 2000000U))
    {
        size_t length = board_can_read(&can_id, frame);
        if ((length > 0U) && (can_id == 0x7E8U))
        {
            isotp_link_receive(&tester, frame, length, board_micros());
        }
        isotp_link_poll(&tester, board_micros());
    }
    return result;
}

with on_answer as on_message and on_error as both on_tx_done and on_rx_error in the tester's configuration (tx_id 0x7E0). A functional request goes to all ECUs at once and must fit a Single Frame:

static struct isotp_link tester;

int tester_present_to_all(void)
{
    static const uint8_t request[2] = {0x3EU, 0x80U};   /* suppress positive response */
    return isotp_link_send_functional(&tester, 0x7DFU, request, sizeof(request));
}

docs.title: Using the codec without a link
docs.text:
The codec is useful on its own, for example in a bus monitor or a gateway that only looks at frames:

void show(const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    struct isotp_pdu pdu;

    if (isotp_decode(data, length, &pdu) == ISOTP_OK)
    {
        if (pdu.type == ISOTP_PCI_FIRST_FRAME)
        {
            /* a message of pdu.message_length bytes starts here */
        }
        else if (pdu.type == ISOTP_PCI_FLOW_CONTROL)
        {
            uint32_t separation_us = isotp_st_min_decode(pdu.st_min);
            (void) separation_us;
        }
        else
        {
            /* Single or Consecutive Frame */
        }
    }
}

docs.text: Function Success Failure isotp_decode() ISOTP_OK ISOTP_ERROR: NULL, length 0 or > 8, malformed frame isotp_encode_*(), isotp_frame_pad() frame length (1..8) ISOTP_ERROR: NULL, value out of range, buffer too small isotp_link_init() ISOTP_OK ISOTP_ERROR: NULL, no writer, value out of range isotp_link_send() ISOTP_OK ISOTP_BUSY, ISOTP_ERROR, or the writer's error isotp_link_send_functional() ISOTP_OK ISOTP_ERROR (longer than 7 bytes), or the writer's error isotp_link_tx_result(), isotp_link_rx_result() ISOTP_N_OK an ISOTP_N_* code

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: Function Tells you isotp_link_tx_busy() A segmented transmission is in progress isotp_link_tx_result() The outcome of the last transmission isotp_link_rx_result() The outcome of the last reception (also ISOTP_N_UNEXP_PDU when a new request interrupted one) isotp_link_invalid_frames() How many malformed frames were ignored — a high count points to wrong CAN ID routing or a peer with another addressing mode

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause Single Frames work, long messages time out at the peer (N_Bs) Frames of the peer's ID are not passed to isotp_link_receive(), or the Flow Control is sent with the wrong tx_id Long messages stall after the First Frame isotp_link_poll() is not called, or called with a time that does not advance Every transmission ends with ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_BS at once now_us is in milliseconds or wraps at less than 2^32 The peer reports wrong sequence numbers Frames are dropped by a full CAN RX queue; enlarge it or ask for a larger STmin The peer ignores the frames It expects 8-byte frames: set padding isotp_link_invalid_frames() grows Another node's traffic is routed to the link, or the peer uses extended addressing isotp_link_send() returns ISOTP_BUSY forever The previous transmission waits for Flow Control that never comes; it ends after N_Bs

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
A link connects this node to one peer: it sends with the CAN ID isotp_link_config::tx_id and receives the frames the application routes to it (normally the frames with the peer's CAN ID). The link never reads a clock or touches hardware. The integrator passes every received CAN frame to isotp_link_receive, provides the frame writer isotp_can_write_fn, and calls isotp_link_poll regularly; the current time in microseconds is an argument of every call.

Transmission and reception are independent (full duplex). A complete received message is delivered to isotp_link_config::on_message; the end of a transmission is reported to isotp_link_config::on_tx_done.

A link is not thread-safe. Call isotp_link_receive and isotp_link_poll from one context (for example a CAN task, not an interrupt handler) and serialize isotp_link_send with them.

** **

  • Lifecycle: isotp_link_config_default, isotp_link_init.
  • Message flow: isotp_link_receive, isotp_link_send, isotp_link_send_functional, isotp_link_poll.
  • Diagnostics: isotp_link_tx_busy, isotp_link_tx_result, isotp_link_rx_result, isotp_link_invalid_frames.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The codec holds no state. isotp_decode validates one received CAN frame and describes it in a isotp_pdu; the encoders write one frame into a caller buffer and return its length. Frames are classical CAN (up to 8 data bytes) with normal addressing. The encoders produce the shortest frame; isotp_frame_pad fills it up to 8 bytes when the bus requires padding.

** **

  • Decoding: isotp_decode.
  • Encoding: isotp_encode_single, isotp_encode_first, isotp_encode_consecutive, isotp_encode_flow_control, isotp_frame_pad.
  • Separation time: isotp_st_min_encode, isotp_st_min_decode.

docs.title: function isotp_decode
docs.text:
Validate one received CAN frame and describe it. 

int isotp_decode (
    const uint8_t * frame,
    size_t length,
    struct isotp_pdu * pdu
)

Rejects frames that ISO 15765-2 tells a receiver to ignore: unknown frame type, SF_DL of 0 or longer than the frame, a First Frame that is not 8 bytes long or announces a message that would fit a Single Frame (or, with the 32-bit FF_DL, fits the 12-bit field), a Consecutive Frame without data, a Flow Control frame shorter than 3 bytes. The flow status is not checked here: an unknown value is an N_INVALID_FS condition the sender has to report.

Parameters:

  • frame CAN frame data.
  • length CAN data length, 1..8.
  • pdu Receives the description.

Return value:

  • ISOTP_OK pdu describes a valid frame.
  • ISOTP_ERROR NULL argument, invalid length or malformed frame.

uint8_t isotp_st_min_encode (
    uint32_t us
)

Rounds up, so the sender never sends faster than requested: 0 us gives 0x00, 1..900 us give 0xF1..0xF9 (100 us steps), 901..127000 us give 0x01..0x7F (1 ms steps), larger values 0x7F.

Parameters:

  • us Separation time in microseconds.

Returns:

Raw STmin byte.

/* ==============================================================================
 * INCLUDES
 * =============================================================================*/

#include <string.h>

#include "isotp_link.h"

/* ==============================================================================
 * DEFINES & MACROS
 * =============================================================================*/

#define ISOTP_DEFAULT_PADDING_VALUE 0xCCU
#define ISOTP_TIMEOUT_MAX_US 0x7FFFFFFFU /* deadlines are compared modulo 2^32 */
#define ISOTP_TIME_HALF_RANGE 0x80000000U

/* ==============================================================================
 * PRIVATE FUNCTION DECLARATIONS (static)
 * =============================================================================*/

static bool isotp_time_reached(uint32_t now_us, uint32_t deadline_us);
static uint32_t isotp_min_u32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b);
static int isotp_link_write(const struct isotp_link* link, uint32_t can_id, uint8_t* frame,
                            int length);
static int isotp_link_send_fc(const struct isotp_link* link, uint8_t flow_status);
static void isotp_link_tx_finish(struct isotp_link* link, int n_result);
static void isotp_link_rx_fail(struct isotp_link* link, int n_result);
static void isotp_link_rx_interrupt(struct isotp_link* link);
static void isotp_link_rx_single(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* data,
                                 const struct isotp_pdu* pdu);
static void isotp_link_rx_first(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* data,
                                const struct isotp_pdu* pdu, uint32_t now_us);
static void isotp_link_rx_consecutive(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* data,
                                      const struct isotp_pdu* pdu, uint32_t now_us);
static void isotp_link_rx_flow_control(struct isotp_link* link, const struct isotp_pdu* pdu,
                                       uint32_t now_us);
static void isotp_link_tx_consecutive(struct isotp_link* link, uint32_t now_us);

/* ==============================================================================
 * PRIVATE FUNCTION IMPLEMENTATIONS
 * =============================================================================*/

/* True when now_us is at or after deadline_us; valid for distances below 2^31 us. */
static bool isotp_time_reached(uint32_t now_us, uint32_t deadline_us)
{
    return ((uint32_t) (now_us - deadline_us)) < ISOTP_TIME_HALF_RANGE;
}

static uint32_t isotp_min_u32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b)
{
    return (a < b) ? a : b;
}

/*
 * Pad (when configured) and write one encoded frame. The callers pass only
 * lengths returned by a successful encoder call: their arguments are checked
 * before, so the encoders cannot fail here and length is 1..8.
 */
static int isotp_link_write(const struct isotp_link* link, uint32_t can_id, uint8_t* frame,
                            int length)
{
    size_t frame_length = (size_t) length;

    if (link->config.padding)
    {
        frame_length = (size_t) isotp_frame_pad(frame, (size_t) ISOTP_CAN_DL, frame_length,
                                                link->config.padding_value);
    }
    return link->config.write(link->config.write_context, can_id, frame, frame_length);
}

static int isotp_link_send_fc(const struct isotp_link* link, uint8_t flow_status)
{
    uint8_t frame[ISOTP_CAN_DL];
    int length =
        isotp_encode_flow_control(frame, sizeof(frame), flow_status, link->config.block_size,
                                  isotp_st_min_encode(link->config.st_min_us));

    return isotp_link_write(link, link->config.tx_id, frame, length);
}

static void isotp_link_tx_finish(struct isotp_link* link, int n_result)
{
    link->tx_state = ISOTP_TX_IDLE;
    link->tx_result = n_result;
    if (link->config.on_tx_done != NULL)
    {
        link->config.on_tx_done(n_result, link->config.app_context);
    }
}

static void isotp_link_rx_fail(struct isotp_link* link, int n_result)
{
    link->rx_state = ISOTP_RX_IDLE;
    link->rx_result = n_result;
    if (link->config.on_rx_error != NULL)
    {
        link->config.on_rx_error(n_result, link->config.app_context);
    }
}

/* A new SF or FF ends a reception in progress (N_UNEXP_PDU) and is processed. */
static void isotp_link_rx_interrupt(struct isotp_link* link)
{
    if (link->rx_state == ISOTP_RX_RECEIVING)
    {
        isotp_link_rx_fail(link, ISOTP_N_UNEXP_PDU);
    }
}

static void isotp_link_rx_single(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* data,
                                 const struct isotp_pdu* pdu)
{
    isotp_link_rx_interrupt(link);
    link->rx_result = ISOTP_N_OK;
    if (link->config.on_message != NULL)
    {
        link->config.on_message(&data[pdu->data_offset], pdu->message_length,
                                link->config.app_context);
    }
}

static void isotp_link_rx_first(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* data,
                                const struct isotp_pdu* pdu, uint32_t now_us)
{
    isotp_link_rx_interrupt(link);

    if (pdu->message_length > ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE)
    {
        /* The sender aborts on OVFLW; nothing to retry if this write fails */
        (void) isotp_link_send_fc(link, ISOTP_FS_OVERFLOW);
        isotp_link_rx_fail(link, ISOTP_N_BUFFER_OVFLW);
    }
    else
    {
        /* data_length is 6 or 2 and message_length > 7, so the copy fits the buffer */
        (void) memcpy(link->rx_buffer, &data[pdu->data_offset], (size_t) pdu->data_length);
        link->rx_size = pdu->message_length;
        link->rx_offset = pdu->data_length;
        link->rx_sn = ISOTP_FIRST_SN;
        link->rx_block_count = link->config.block_size;

        if (isotp_link_send_fc(link, ISOTP_FS_CONTINUE) == ISOTP_OK)
        {
            link->rx_state = ISOTP_RX_RECEIVING;
            link->rx_deadline_us = now_us + link->config.n_cr_timeout_us;
        }
        else
        {
            isotp_link_rx_fail(link, ISOTP_N_ERROR);
        }
    }
}

static void isotp_link_rx_consecutive(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* data,
                                      const struct isotp_pdu* pdu, uint32_t now_us)
{
    if (link->rx_state != ISOTP_RX_RECEIVING)
    {
        /* Not expecting a Consecutive Frame: ISO 15765-2 says ignore it */
    }
    else if (pdu->sequence_number != link->rx_sn)
    {
        isotp_link_rx_fail(link, ISOTP_N_WRONG_SN);
    }
    else
    {
        uint32_t take = isotp_min_u32(link->rx_size - link->rx_offset, ISOTP_CF_MAX_DATA);

        if ((uint32_t) pdu->data_length < take)
        {
            /* Too short for the bytes still expected */
            link->invalid_frames++;
        }
        else
        {
            /* rx_offset + take <= rx_size <= ISOTP_RX_BUFFER_SIZE */
            (void) memcpy(&link->rx_buffer[link->rx_offset], &data[pdu->data_offset],
                          (size_t) take);
            link->rx_offset += take;
            link->rx_sn = (uint8_t) ((link->rx_sn + 1U) & ISOTP_SN_MASK);
            link->rx_deadline_us = now_us + link->config.n_cr_timeout_us;

            if (link->rx_offset == link->rx_size)
            {
                link->rx_state = ISOTP_RX_IDLE;
                link->rx_result = ISOTP_N_OK;
                if (link->config.on_message != NULL)
                {
                    link->config.on_message(link->rx_buffer, link->rx_size,
                                            link->config.app_context);
                }
            }
            else if (link->config.block_size != 0U)
            {
                link->rx_block_count--;
                if (link->rx_block_count == 0U)
                {
                    link->rx_block_count = link->config.block_size;
                    if (isotp_link_send_fc(link, ISOTP_FS_CONTINUE) != ISOTP_OK)
                    {
                        isotp_link_rx_fail(link, ISOTP_N_ERROR);
                    }
                }
            }
            else
            {
                /* BS = 0: the sender continues without further Flow Control */
            }
        }
    }
}

static void isotp_link_rx_flow_control(struct isotp_link* link, const struct isotp_pdu* pdu,
                                       uint32_t now_us)
{
    if (link->tx_state != ISOTP_TX_WAIT_FC)
    {
        /* Not waiting for Flow Control: ISO 15765-2 says ignore it */
    }
    else if (pdu->flow_status == ISOTP_FS_CONTINUE)
    {
        link->tx_block_unlimited = (pdu->block_size == 0U);
        link->tx_block_remaining = pdu->block_size;
        link->tx_st_min_us = isotp_st_min_decode(pdu->st_min);
        link->tx_wft_count = 0U;
        link->tx_state = ISOTP_TX_SEND_CF;
        link->tx_deadline_us = now_us; /* the first CF of a block may follow at once */
    }
    else if (pdu->flow_status == ISOTP_FS_WAIT)
    {
        if (link->tx_wft_count < link->config.wft_max)
        {
            link->tx_wft_count++;
            link->tx_deadline_us = now_us + link->config.n_bs_timeout_us;
        }
        else
        {
            isotp_link_tx_finish(link, ISOTP_N_WFT_OVRN);
        }
    }
    else if (pdu->flow_status == ISOTP_FS_OVERFLOW)
    {
        isotp_link_tx_finish(link, ISOTP_N_BUFFER_OVFLW);
    }
    else
    {
        isotp_link_tx_finish(link, ISOTP_N_INVALID_FS);
    }
}

static void isotp_link_tx_consecutive(struct isotp_link* link, uint32_t now_us)
{
    uint8_t frame[ISOTP_CAN_DL];
    uint32_t take = isotp_min_u32(link->tx_size - link->tx_offset, ISOTP_CF_MAX_DATA);
    int length = isotp_encode_consecutive(frame, sizeof(frame), link->tx_sn,
                                          &link->tx_buffer[link->tx_offset], take);
    int written = isotp_link_write(link, link->config.tx_id, frame, length);

    if (written == ISOTP_OK)
    {
        link->tx_offset += take;
        link->tx_sn = (uint8_t) ((link->tx_sn + 1U) & ISOTP_SN_MASK);
        link->tx_deadline_us = now_us + link->tx_st_min_us;

        if (link->tx_offset == link->tx_size)
        {
            isotp_link_tx_finish(link, ISOTP_N_OK);
        }
        else if (!link->tx_block_unlimited)
        {
            /* tx_block_remaining >= 1 here: BS > 0 and the block is not finished */
            link->tx_block_remaining--;
            if (link->tx_block_remaining == 0U)
            {
                link->tx_state = ISOTP_TX_WAIT_FC;
                link->tx_deadline_us = now_us + link->config.n_bs_timeout_us;
            }
        }
        else
        {
            /* BS = 0: keep sending */
        }
    }
    else if (written == ISOTP_BUSY)
    {
        /* Driver queue full: retry on the next poll */
    }
    else
    {
        isotp_link_tx_finish(link, ISOTP_N_ERROR);
    }
}

/* ==============================================================================
 * PUBLIC FUNCTION IMPLEMENTATIONS
 * =============================================================================*/

void isotp_link_config_default(struct isotp_link_config* config)
{
    if (config != NULL)
    {
        config->tx_id = 0U;
        config->write = NULL;
        config->write_context = NULL;
        config->on_message = NULL;
        config->on_tx_done = NULL;
        config->on_rx_error = NULL;
        config->app_context = NULL;
        config->block_size = (uint8_t) ISOTP_DEFAULT_BLOCK_SIZE;
        config->st_min_us = ISOTP_DEFAULT_ST_MIN_US;
        config->n_bs_timeout_us = ISOTP_DEFAULT_N_BS_TIMEOUT_US;
        config->n_cr_timeout_us = ISOTP_DEFAULT_N_CR_TIMEOUT_US;
        config->wft_max = (uint8_t) ISOTP_DEFAULT_WFT_MAX;
        config->padding = false;
        config->padding_value = ISOTP_DEFAULT_PADDING_VALUE;
    }
}

int isotp_link_init(struct isotp_link* link, const struct isotp_link_config* config)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((link != NULL) && (config != NULL) && (config->write != NULL)
        && (config->st_min_us <= ISOTP_ST_MIN_MAX_US) && (config->n_bs_timeout_us > 0U)
        && (config->n_bs_timeout_us <= ISOTP_TIMEOUT_MAX_US) && (config->n_cr_timeout_us > 0U)
        && (config->n_cr_timeout_us <= ISOTP_TIMEOUT_MAX_US))
    {
        (void) memset(link, 0, sizeof(*link));
        link->config = *config;
        link->tx_state = ISOTP_TX_IDLE;
        link->rx_state = ISOTP_RX_IDLE;
        link->tx_result = ISOTP_N_OK;
        link->rx_result = ISOTP_N_OK;
        result = ISOTP_OK;
    }
    return result;
}

void isotp_link_receive(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* data, size_t length,
                        uint32_t now_us)
{
    struct isotp_pdu pdu;

    if (link != NULL)
    {
        if (isotp_decode(data, length, &pdu) != ISOTP_OK)
        {
            link->invalid_frames++;
        }
        else if (pdu.type == ISOTP_PCI_SINGLE_FRAME)
        {
            isotp_link_rx_single(link, data, &pdu);
        }
        else if (pdu.type == ISOTP_PCI_FIRST_FRAME)
        {
            isotp_link_rx_first(link, data, &pdu, now_us);
        }
        else if (pdu.type == ISOTP_PCI_CONSECUTIVE_FRAME)
        {
            isotp_link_rx_consecutive(link, data, &pdu, now_us);
        }
        else
        {
            /* isotp_decode accepts only the four frame types: this is Flow Control */
            isotp_link_rx_flow_control(link, &pdu, now_us);
        }
    }
}

int isotp_link_send(struct isotp_link* link, const uint8_t* payload, uint32_t length,
                    uint32_t now_us)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;
    uint8_t frame[ISOTP_CAN_DL];

    if ((link == NULL) || (payload == NULL) || (length == 0U) || (length > ISOTP_TX_BUFFER_SIZE))
    {
        /* result stays ISOTP_ERROR */
    }
    else if (link->tx_state != ISOTP_TX_IDLE)
    {
        result = ISOTP_BUSY;
    }
    else if (length <= ISOTP_SF_MAX_DL)
    {
        int frame_length = isotp_encode_single(frame, sizeof(frame), payload, length);

        result = isotp_link_write(link, link->config.tx_id, frame, frame_length);
        if (result == ISOTP_OK)
        {
            isotp_link_tx_finish(link, ISOTP_N_OK);
        }
    }
    else
    {
        int frame_length;

        (void) memcpy(link->tx_buffer, payload, (size_t) length);
        frame_length = isotp_encode_first(frame, sizeof(frame), link->tx_buffer, length);
        result = isotp_link_write(link, link->config.tx_id, frame, frame_length);
        if (result == ISOTP_OK)
        {
            link->tx_size = length;
            link->tx_offset = (length <= ISOTP_FF_DL_12BIT_MAX) ? (uint32_t) ISOTP_FF_SHORT_DATA :
                                                                  (uint32_t) ISOTP_FF_LONG_DATA;
            link->tx_sn = ISOTP_FIRST_SN;
            link->tx_wft_count = 0U;
            link->tx_state = ISOTP_TX_WAIT_FC;
            link->tx_deadline_us = now_us + link->config.n_bs_timeout_us;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

int isotp_link_send_functional(const struct isotp_link* link, uint32_t can_id,
                               const uint8_t* payload, uint32_t length)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((link != NULL) && (payload != NULL) && (length > 0U) && (length <= ISOTP_SF_MAX_DL))
    {
        uint8_t frame[ISOTP_CAN_DL];
        int frame_length = isotp_encode_single(frame, sizeof(frame), payload, length);

        result = isotp_link_write(link, can_id, frame, frame_length);
    }
    return result;
}

void isotp_link_poll(struct isotp_link* link, uint32_t now_us)
{
    if (link != NULL)
    {
        if (link->tx_state == ISOTP_TX_IDLE)
        {
            /* nothing to send */
        }
        else if (!isotp_time_reached(now_us, link->tx_deadline_us))
        {
            /* waiting for Flow Control or for STmin */
        }
        else if (link->tx_state == ISOTP_TX_WAIT_FC)
        {
            isotp_link_tx_finish(link, ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_BS);
        }
        else
        {
            isotp_link_tx_consecutive(link, now_us);
        }

        if ((link->rx_state == ISOTP_RX_RECEIVING)
            && isotp_time_reached(now_us, link->rx_deadline_us))
        {
            isotp_link_rx_fail(link, ISOTP_N_TIMEOUT_CR);
        }
    }
}

/* ==============================================================================
 * INCLUDES
 * =============================================================================*/

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "isotp_protocol.h"

/* ==============================================================================
 * DEFINES & MACROS
 * =============================================================================*/

#define ISOTP_PCI_TYPE_SHIFT 4U   /* frame type is the high nibble of byte 0 */
#define ISOTP_LOW_NIBBLE 0x0FU    /* SF_DL, FF_DL high bits, SN and FS */
#define ISOTP_FF_SHORT_OFFSET 2U  /* first payload byte with the 12-bit FF_DL */
#define ISOTP_FF_ESCAPE_OFFSET 6U /* first payload byte with the 32-bit FF_DL */
#define ISOTP_ST_MIN_MS_MAX 0x7FU /* 0x00..0x7F: milliseconds */
#define ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_FIRST 0xF1U
#define ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_LAST 0xF9U
#define ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_BASE 0xF0U
#define ISOTP_US_PER_MS 1000U
#define ISOTP_US_PER_STEP 100U
#define ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_STEPS_MAX 900U

/* ==============================================================================
 * PRIVATE FUNCTION DECLARATIONS (static)
 * =============================================================================*/

static void isotp_pdu_clear(struct isotp_pdu* pdu);
static bool isotp_decode_single(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu);
static bool isotp_decode_first(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu);
static bool isotp_decode_consecutive(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu);
static bool isotp_decode_flow_control(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu);

/* ==============================================================================
 * PRIVATE FUNCTION IMPLEMENTATIONS
 * =============================================================================*/

static void isotp_pdu_clear(struct isotp_pdu* pdu)
{
    pdu->type = 0U;
    pdu->message_length = 0U;
    pdu->data_offset = 0U;
    pdu->data_length = 0U;
    pdu->sequence_number = 0U;
    pdu->flow_status = 0U;
    pdu->block_size = 0U;
    pdu->st_min = 0U;
}

static bool isotp_decode_single(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu)
{
    uint8_t sf_dl = (uint8_t) (frame[0] & ISOTP_LOW_NIBBLE);
    bool valid = (sf_dl > 0U) && ((size_t) sf_dl < length);

    if (valid)
    {
        pdu->message_length = sf_dl;
        pdu->data_offset = 1U;
        pdu->data_length = sf_dl;
    }
    return valid;
}

static bool isotp_decode_first(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu)
{
    bool valid = (length == (size_t) ISOTP_CAN_DL);

    if (valid)
    {
        uint32_t ff_dl = (((uint32_t) frame[0] & ISOTP_LOW_NIBBLE) << 8U) | (uint32_t) frame[1];

        if (ff_dl == 0U)
        {
            /* Escape sequence: 32-bit FF_DL in bytes 2..5, only for long messages */
            ff_dl = isotp_get_u32_be(&frame[ISOTP_FF_SHORT_OFFSET]);
            valid = (ff_dl > ISOTP_FF_DL_12BIT_MAX);
            pdu->data_offset = ISOTP_FF_ESCAPE_OFFSET;
            pdu->data_length = ISOTP_FF_LONG_DATA;
        }
        else
        {
            /* A message that fits a Single Frame must not be segmented */
            valid = (ff_dl > ISOTP_SF_MAX_DL);
            pdu->data_offset = ISOTP_FF_SHORT_OFFSET;
            pdu->data_length = ISOTP_FF_SHORT_DATA;
        }
        pdu->message_length = ff_dl;
    }
    return valid;
}

static bool isotp_decode_consecutive(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu)
{
    bool valid = (length > 1U);

    if (valid)
    {
        pdu->sequence_number = (uint8_t) (frame[0] & ISOTP_LOW_NIBBLE);
        pdu->data_offset = 1U;
        pdu->data_length = (uint8_t) (length - 1U);
    }
    return valid;
}

static bool isotp_decode_flow_control(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu)
{
    bool valid = (length >= (size_t) ISOTP_FC_DL);

    if (valid)
    {
        pdu->flow_status = (uint8_t) (frame[0] & ISOTP_LOW_NIBBLE);
        pdu->block_size = frame[1];
        pdu->st_min = frame[2];
    }
    return valid;
}

/* ==============================================================================
 * PUBLIC FUNCTION IMPLEMENTATIONS
 * =============================================================================*/

int isotp_decode(const uint8_t* frame, size_t length, struct isotp_pdu* pdu)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((frame != NULL) && (pdu != NULL) && (length > 0U) && (length <= (size_t) ISOTP_CAN_DL))
    {
        uint8_t type = (uint8_t) (frame[0] >> ISOTP_PCI_TYPE_SHIFT);
        bool valid = false;

        isotp_pdu_clear(pdu);
        pdu->type = type;

        switch (type)
        {
            case ISOTP_PCI_SINGLE_FRAME:
                valid = isotp_decode_single(frame, length, pdu);
                break;
            case ISOTP_PCI_FIRST_FRAME:
                valid = isotp_decode_first(frame, length, pdu);
                break;
            case ISOTP_PCI_CONSECUTIVE_FRAME:
                valid = isotp_decode_consecutive(frame, length, pdu);
                break;
            case ISOTP_PCI_FLOW_CONTROL:
                valid = isotp_decode_flow_control(frame, length, pdu);
                break;
            default:
                /* Reserved frame types are ignored by the receiver */
                break;
        }

        if (valid)
        {
            result = ISOTP_OK;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

int isotp_encode_single(uint8_t* frame, size_t capacity, const uint8_t* payload, uint32_t length)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((frame != NULL) && (payload != NULL) && (length > 0U) && (length <= ISOTP_SF_MAX_DL)
        && (capacity > (size_t) length))
    {
        frame[0] = (uint8_t) ((ISOTP_PCI_SINGLE_FRAME << ISOTP_PCI_TYPE_SHIFT) | length);
        (void) memcpy(&frame[1], payload, (size_t) length);
        result = (int) length + 1;
    }
    return result;
}

int isotp_encode_first(uint8_t* frame, size_t capacity, const uint8_t* payload,
                       uint32_t message_length)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((frame != NULL) && (payload != NULL) && (message_length > ISOTP_SF_MAX_DL)
        && (capacity >= (size_t) ISOTP_CAN_DL))
    {
        if (message_length <= ISOTP_FF_DL_12BIT_MAX)
        {
            frame[0] = (uint8_t) ((ISOTP_PCI_FIRST_FRAME << ISOTP_PCI_TYPE_SHIFT)
                                  | (message_length >> 8U));
            frame[1] = (uint8_t) (message_length & 0xFFU);
            (void) memcpy(&frame[ISOTP_FF_SHORT_OFFSET], payload, (size_t) ISOTP_FF_SHORT_DATA);
        }
        else
        {
            frame[0] = (uint8_t) (ISOTP_PCI_FIRST_FRAME << ISOTP_PCI_TYPE_SHIFT);
            frame[1] = 0U;
            isotp_put_u32_be(&frame[ISOTP_FF_SHORT_OFFSET], message_length);
            (void) memcpy(&frame[ISOTP_FF_ESCAPE_OFFSET], payload, (size_t) ISOTP_FF_LONG_DATA);
        }
        result = (int) ISOTP_CAN_DL;
    }
    return result;
}

int isotp_encode_consecutive(uint8_t* frame, size_t capacity, uint8_t sequence_number,
                             const uint8_t* data, uint32_t length)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((frame != NULL) && (data != NULL) && (sequence_number <= ISOTP_SN_MASK) && (length > 0U)
        && (length <= ISOTP_CF_MAX_DATA) && (capacity > (size_t) length))
    {
        frame[0] = (uint8_t) ((ISOTP_PCI_CONSECUTIVE_FRAME << ISOTP_PCI_TYPE_SHIFT)
                              | (uint32_t) sequence_number);
        (void) memcpy(&frame[1], data, (size_t) length);
        result = (int) length + 1;
    }
    return result;
}

int isotp_encode_flow_control(uint8_t* frame, size_t capacity, uint8_t flow_status,
                              uint8_t block_size, uint8_t st_min)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((frame != NULL) && (flow_status <= ISOTP_FS_OVERFLOW) && (capacity >= (size_t) ISOTP_FC_DL))
    {
        frame[0] =
            (uint8_t) ((ISOTP_PCI_FLOW_CONTROL << ISOTP_PCI_TYPE_SHIFT) | (uint32_t) flow_status);
        frame[1] = block_size;
        frame[2] = st_min;
        result = (int) ISOTP_FC_DL;
    }
    return result;
}

int isotp_frame_pad(uint8_t* frame, size_t capacity, size_t length, uint8_t value)
{
    int result = ISOTP_ERROR;

    if ((frame != NULL) && (capacity >= (size_t) ISOTP_CAN_DL) && (length > 0U)
        && (length <= (size_t) ISOTP_CAN_DL))
    {
        (void) memset(&frame[length], (int) value, (size_t) ISOTP_CAN_DL - length);
        result = (int) ISOTP_CAN_DL;
    }
    return result;
}

uint8_t isotp_st_min_encode(uint32_t us)
{
    uint8_t result;

    if (us == 0U)
    {
        result = 0U;
    }
    else if (us <= ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_STEPS_MAX)
    {
        /* 100 us steps, rounded up */
        result = (uint8_t) (ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_BASE
                            + ((us + (ISOTP_US_PER_STEP - 1U)) / ISOTP_US_PER_STEP));
    }
    else if (us < ISOTP_ST_MIN_MAX_US)
    {
        /* 1 ms steps, rounded up */
        result = (uint8_t) ((us + (ISOTP_US_PER_MS - 1U)) / ISOTP_US_PER_MS);
    }
    else
    {
        result = ISOTP_ST_MIN_MS_MAX;
    }
    return result;
}

uint32_t isotp_st_min_decode(uint8_t st_min)
{
    uint32_t result;

    if (st_min <= ISOTP_ST_MIN_MS_MAX)
    {
        result = (uint32_t) st_min * ISOTP_US_PER_MS;
    }
    else if ((st_min >= ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_FIRST) && (st_min <= ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_LAST))
    {
        result = ((uint32_t) st_min - ISOTP_ST_MIN_US_BASE) * ISOTP_US_PER_STEP;
    }
    else
    {
        /* Reserved values: ISO 15765-2 requires the longest time, 127 ms */
        result = ISOTP_ST_MIN_MAX_US;
    }
    return result;
}
